s: oops

Uppsala.et: Borrowed from Swedish Uppsala, from Old Norse Uppsalir (literally “upper halls, upper dwellings”), from upp (“up”) + salir (“halls, rooms”, plural of salr).

s: oopsy-daisy, oh dear.
humorous
Die schöne TV-Gesangslehrerin zur B.Z.: „Es ist ein Uppsala-Baby. Wir dachten: Was ist denn da passiert?!“
The beautiful TV singing teacher said to B.Z.: "It's an oopsy-daisy-baby. We thought: what's happened here?!"
Er zertrümmerte einer Bestie den Schädel – sagte »Uppsala!« – und schleuderte eine weitere durch die Luft

Uppsala.et: Blend of ups (“oops”) + hoppala (“oops”), influenced by the Swedish city.

s: opulent, luscious, ample
üppig.et: From Middle High German üppic, from Old High German uppīg, further origin uncertain, perhaps related to übel.

s: lavishly, lushly

üppig.et: From Middle High German üppic, from Old High German uppīg, further origin uncertain, perhaps related to übel.
